neighbours.label: a comparison marker introducing a likeness or contrast clause (Like, Unlike, Similar to, Just like)
fire: The debate is old. Unlike state elections, it is not decided by voters.
Similar to how running builds the heart, reading builds the mind.
Just like you train your legs, you have to train your memory.
Many women worry about this. Like most mothers, I want answers.
Teachers face long hours. Like nurses, they often work at night.
The disease is complex, unlike those found in other organs.
Much like a garden, a friendship needs regular care.
Unlike its rivals, the small firm refused to raise prices.
quiet: The debate is old. State elections, however, are decided by voters.
Running builds the heart, and reading builds the mind.
You train your legs, and you also have to train your memory.
Many women worry about this. As a mother, I want answers.
Teachers face long hours. They often work at night as well.
The disease is complex and affects several different organs.
A friendship needs regular care to stay healthy and strong.
The small firm refused to raise prices this year.
